tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/password-hashing.md <<'EOF'
# Password hashing

The project's current recorded decision is to hash passwords with argon2id. The reason given for choosing it is that it resists GPU-based attacks much better than the algorithm it replaced. No cost parameters (memory, iterations, parallelism) are recorded, so none are specified here.
EOF
cat docs/policies/password-hashing.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/password-hashing.md` with a one-paragraph statement that the project's current recorded decision is argon2id. The reason it gives is the recorded one: argon2id resists GPU attacks much better. The paragraph also says that no cost parameters are recorded, so it doesn't specify any. It doesn't mention the algorithm that was replaced.

Muninn flags the argon2id decision (#19) as in conflict with #9. I checked #9, and it's about an async runtime (async-std), so it doesn't affect the password hashing decision.

The first attempt to write the file through Bash failed with a parser error. I wrote it with the Write tool instead.
